_comment: A&B Motors' merchandising policy, read by CoreYard through STORE_PROFILE_FILE.
CoreYard renders every product's title, description, SEO metadata and tags, but it
ships neutral defaults that claim only what the yard database can prove. The claims
below are ours: we do assess and grade parts when a donor is catalogued, and we pull,
inspect and clean them before they ship. See _availability: most parts are still on
the donor when they are listed, so the second check is the one that happens on order.
A yard that does not do that must not
inherit the wording, which is why it lives here and not in CoreYard.
Every string is TEXT, never HTML — CoreYard escapes what it is given and owns the
markup. {part_type} and {origin} are substituted; {origin} is 'A&B Motors, <city>',
built from SHOPIFY_VENDOR and STORE_CITY in the backend's .env.
CHANGING ANY OF THIS REPUBLISHES THE CATALOG. These strings are part of the rendered
product, and the rendered product is what the sync fingerprints, so an edit here makes
the next run rewrite every product it touches. Run `bin/coreyard --sink api --dry-run`
body_lead: Genuine OEM {part_type} from an inventoried donor vehicle at our yard, pulled and inspected before it leaves the lot.
fitment_note: Verify fitment by year, options, and part/casting numbers where shown in the photos.

part_type_notices.air bag: This is a used, vehicle-specific air bag removed from a salvage vehicle; its prior replacement history has not been independently verified. A deployed air bag cannot be reused. Have an authorized repair facility verify its condition, OEM part number, vehicle compatibility, donor history, and recall status before installation.

_metafields: CoreYard publishes the structured half of a listing as metafields in this
namespace: grade, mileage, condition, and fitment. The theme reads them as
product.metafields.abm.* — the spec table renders every non-fitment key it
finds, and the 'Fits these vehicles' table reads abm.fitment. Renaming this
orphans every metafield already on the store, so it is chosen once.
CoreYard's own default is 'coreyard'; 'abm' is ours because the theme was
written against it before CoreYard published anything here.
_availability: Most of the yard is still on the donor vehicle when it is listed: 23,268 of 28,718
available parts sit in a yard section (SY-A..SY-G, A, AB, M, YARD) rather than a bin or
a rack, and 98.6% of live listings show donor-vehicle photographs because the part was
never photographed on its own. So the part is in stock and it is ours, but it has not
been pulled or inspected yet — that happens when the order comes in.
'In stock and inspected' and 'removed from ... and inspected' both claimed otherwise on
every listing, against a product page that says the photos are of the donor vehicle.
The storefront now says the same thing everywhere: on our lot, pulled and inspected
This republishes every product. See the note at the top of this file.
_title: OEM stays out of the customer-facing title on purpose. It is a high-intent search term,
but the title is already carrying the vehicles and a part type, and Google reads the
SEO description and the tags too — where OEM appears either way.
title_max_models 0 means 'as many vehicles as the character budget holds' rather than a
fixed count. The budget is the destination's own: 255 characters on Shopify, 80 on the
listing portal, so one setting fills a long title and still fits a short one.
At the old cap of 4, 2,663 live titles spent characters on the phrase 'and 17 more'
instead of naming a car, suppressing 15,145 vehicle names across the catalogue. Those
names are the exact long-tail searches this yard wins on ('2009 Saturn Outlook ABS
pump'). Mean title length goes from about 91 characters to about 124.
The SEO/meta title is a separate 60-character field and is unaffected: it is what
Google shows as the blue link, and it stays short on purpose.
This republishes every multi-vehicle title. See the note at the top of this file.
_title_grade: The yard's own A/B/C grade, in the title as 'A Grade'. It is a fact about the record,
not a claim about the part: whatever was entered is what is published. It is also a
metafield and a line in the description either way, so this only decides the title.
Catalogue spread today: A 17,550, C 1,895, B 605, ungraded 6,808. An ungraded part
_title_mileage: Donor mileage in the title, but only where mileage is what a buyer judges the part by.
The source system stamps the donor's odometer on every part pulled from it, so a door
glass carries a mileage as surely as the engine does -- and on the glass it is noise.
The list below is drivetrain and rotating/pumping wear items. Add or remove a line and
the next repair pass rewrites those titles; nothing else has to change. Part types are
the source system's own spelling, lower-cased.
title_mileage_max is 200000: at or under it the number sells the part, above it the
number argues against it and we would rather say nothing. Mileage is rendered in
thousands ('142K Miles') because the exact figure needs a comma, and a comma is one of
_tags: ship:* tags are written by scripts/tag_shipping.py and read by the theme to warn a
shopper before checkout. CoreYard preserves any namespaced tag automatically, so they
survive every catalog update without being named here; the list below is belt and
braces, and documents the ownership boundary for anyone reading this file.
_audit: Thresholds for `bin/coreyard audit catalog`. Audit-only: none of these reach the
rendered product, so editing them never republishes anything.
min_price is 5 because nothing in the yard is genuinely worth less than that, so a
sub-$5 listing is a data error rather than a bargain. min_description_chars matches
the shortest description CoreYard produces for a part with no fitment rows.
min_title_chars is 15, not 25. A real title here is '<year> <make> <part type>' and
the shortest legitimate ones run 18 characters ('2007 Cadillac Glove Box'). At 25 the
audit flagged 64 perfectly good listings, and an audit that cries wolf is one nobody
reads. A genuinely broken title -- one that lost its fitment -- is far shorter.
